To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existing cache replacement policies, which are well optimized to minimize the I/O traffic, are insufficient to address the GC problem and the contention between the user I/ O requests and the GC-induced I/O operations within flash-based SSDs.

we propose and implement GCaR, a new cache management scheme that is specifically designed to reduce the expensive I/O requests to the flash chips in the GC state, by using a new replacement algorithm that is based on a new cost model.

1) the existing cache replacement policies are not sufficient and effective in alleviating the GC-induced performance degradation of flash-based SSDs; 2) the proposed cache replacement policy, named GCaR (Garbage Collection aware Cache Replacement policy), is able to effectively alleviate the GC-induced performance problem of flash-based SSD.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and implementation of a novel GC-aware cache replacement algorithm for the on-board buffer cache of SSDs to reduce the I/O traffic and the associated latency to the flash chips in the GC state, and to improve the overall performance of flash-based SSDs.

the design and implementation of an efficient and effective cache management mechanism to reduce the expensive I/O operations that are triggered by the GC state within the flash chips, while still maintaining high performance for normal I/O traffic to SSDs.
the following questions: How can we effectively reduce the I/O traffic that is generated by the GC operations and the user I/O traffic that are mutually interfering with each other?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the existing cache replacement schemes are well optimized to the I/O traffic from the upper-level applications, but are far from being optimized to the I-O traffic from the GC state.
the existing cache replacement policies are not well optimized to reduce I/O traffic to flash chips in the GC state and thus cannot effectively address this problem.
, in spite of its great potential, the on-board buffer cache is not well utilized to its fullest extent in the existing cache replacement policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a GC-aware buffer replacement scheme that can effectively reduce the GC traffic to the flash chip and improve the overall performance of flash-based SSDs.
we have designed and developed GCaR, a new cache replacement algorithm that is aware of GC operations within SSDs.
we have developed a novel GC-aware cache management scheme, called GCaR, that can effectively reduce the I/O traffic of GC-induced I/Os and thus improve the SSD performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we propose a novel cache replacement algorithm, called GCaR, to reduce the expensive I/Os to the flash chips by considering the GC operations in the flash chips.

, in order to reduce the expensive I/O requests to the flash chips in the GC state, it is necessary and important to consider the GC operations within flash chips when designing the cache management algorithms for the buffer cache within SSD.
, the existing cache management algorithms should take into consideration the GC operations in flash chips and thus be GC-aware in order to achieve the best performance of SSDs.
